status: frozen v1 contract with encoder comparison rule v2 (see comparison_rules.encoder_revision_reason). Native Linux ARM64 re-observation (run v2, pinned FFmpeg 9.0.2 gating build): conversion within ±1 with the same exact-match fractions as the macOS exploration, PAT bytes equal, PMT equal apart from the stream_type decision, SDT apart from the SDT decision, per-frame PTS/DTS/PCR and table cadence as stated, and the reference's one-frame output delay (89 reference pictures for 90 inputs) in all 15 cases.
operation_source: The capture call sequence of an application that streams its interface as MPEG-1 video in MPEG-TS: RGBA converted to NV12 by swscale (SWS_BILINEAR, negative stride for bottom-up rows), NV12 split into YUV420P planes, mpeg1video with time base 1/30, GOP 30, no B-pictures and fastint DCT, frame pts 0, 1, 2, ..., mpegts muxed through a 32,768-byte custom AVIO, av_write_frame and avio_flush per frame, no trailer. A rate byte times 100 kbps selects the bit rate (0 selects 2.5 Mbps); a width of at least 720 (or 0) selects 960x540, otherwise 480x270. harness/reference_capture.h reproduces this sequence.

reference.configuration: the application's development component set with --enable-small, and the same set without it as the gating build; built natively on the qualification host, exact argv recorded in the reference build receipt

input.pixel_format: RGBA, 8 bits per channel, byte order R,G,B,A, tightly packed rows (stride = 4*width)
input.orientation: top-down or bottom-up (the application's `flip`); bottom-up is read with a negative stride, no CPU flip pass
input.alpha: ignored (observed: alpha 0 and 255 give identical YUV)
input.frame_cadence: <= 30 fps, jittery; timestamps are frame counts, not capture times

conversion.output: YUV 4:2:0 planar (Y w*h, U and V (w/2)*(h/2)), as handed to the encoder
conversion.range: limited: Y 16-235, Cb/Cr 16-240 (swscale default; no sws_setColorspaceDetails call)
conversion.chroma_horizontal: mean of the two horizontally co-located RGBA pixels (observed swscale chrSrcHSubSample path)
conversion.chroma_vertical: center-sited 2:1 decimation, taps 1/8,3/8,3/8,1/8 on source rows 2k-1..2k+2, edge rows replicated (observed SWS_BILINEAR kernel)
conversion.rounding: not specified normatively; comparison rule bounds the difference
conversion.observed_on: macOS ARM64 Homebrew FFmpeg 9.0.2 (exploratory); to be re-observed on pinned Linux ARM64
conversion.known_platform_divergence: A 32-bit ARM build selects swscale's arm rgbx_to_nv12 NEON converter, whose chroma/rounding may differ from the AArch64 general path. The Linux ARM64 qualification reference is the general path; 32-bit ARM equivalence is not covered here.

encoder.standard: ISO/IEC 11172-2 (MPEG-1 video); normative syntax evidence from freely available ITU-T H.262 (MPEG-1 compatibility) plus public descriptions; no specification purchased
encoder.picture_types: I and P only (bf 0); no B, no D pictures
encoder.gop: intra period 30 frames (g 30); sequence header and GOP header before every I picture; closed GOP
encoder.aspect: pel aspect ratio code 1 (square), matching FFmpeg's default sample_aspect_ratio 0/1 -> 1:1
encoder.motion: full-pel and half-pel forward motion vectors; search algorithm is an implementation choice measured by the quality gate
encoder.dct: fastint is FFmpeg's DCT implementation selector; any IEEE-1180-accurate forward DCT is acceptable for the quality gate
encoder.quantisation: default MPEG-1 intra matrix, flat 16 non-intra matrix, qscale 2..31
encoder.latency: FFmpeg 9.0.2 emits frame k's bytes only when frame k+1 is sent (observed: 1 frame -> 0 bytes, 2 frames -> 1 packet) and never emits the last frame (no drain, no trailer). The replacement emits frame k at call k. A deliberate difference (lower latency, same per-frame timestamps), approved under decisions.
encoder.constrained_parameters_flag: 0 for both geometries (960x540 and 480x270 exceed 11172-2 constrained parameter limits)

timestamps.time_base_90khz: frame k of a session: DTS = 3000*k, PTS = 3000*(k+1) (observed FFmpeg values after its non-negative shift; PTS-DTS one frame period is the MPEG-1 anchor-picture reorder delay)
timestamps.pcr: 27 MHz PCR = DTS*300 on the first TS packet of every PES (VBR mode, max_delay 0)
timestamps.session_restart: new session restarts k at 0, continuity counters at 0, tables at version 0

mux.standard: ITU-T H.222.0 | ISO/IEC 13818-1 transport stream (freely available ITU-T text)
mux.stream_type: observed 0x02 (FFmpeg maps MPEG-1 video to H.262 type). H.222.0 Table 2-34 assigns 0x01 to ISO/IEC 11172-2 video and limits 0x02's 11172-2 use to constrained-parameter streams, which these are not. Replacement default 0x01; 0x02 selectable. A deliberate difference, approved under decisions.
mux.sdt: service descriptor, service_type 0x01, provider/service names: FFmpeg writes 'FFmpeg'/'Service01'. Replacement default provider 'Triergon', service 'Service01', both selectable. A deliberate metadata difference, approved under decisions.
mux.table_cadence: SDT on the first packet and when PCR advanced >= 500 ms since the last SDT; PAT+PMT on the first packet, when PCR advanced >= 100 ms since the last PAT, and before a key-frame PES whose predecessor was not a key frame; order SDT, PAT, PMT, then the PES
mux.pes: stream_id 0xE0, PES_packet_length 0, '10' marker, no data alignment flag, PTS+DTS (both always present because PTS != DTS), header_data_length 10, one PES per encoded picture
mux.adaptation: first TS packet of each PES carries an adaptation field with PCR; random_access_indicator set on key-frame PES; stuffing in the adaptation field of the final packet
mux.continuity: per-PID 4-bit counter incremented on every payload-bearing packet
mux.output_chunks: FFmpeg writes through a 32768-byte AVIO buffer flushed per frame; chunk boundaries are not semantic (TCP byte stream). The replacement hands each frame's complete TS bytes to the sink.
mux.write_failure: a sink failure or partial write fails the frame; the caller drops the client and rebuilds a fresh session

session.open: fresh encoder+muxer per client/restart: first output is SDT, PAT, PMT then a sequence-header I picture
session.rebuild: consumer policy (geometry change, >1500 ms gap, write failure) - outside the library
session.keepalive: consumer re-encodes the last picture; library guarantees advancing PTS/DTS/PCR and continuity on every call
session.outside_scope: GLES readback, sockets, hello protocol, JPEG mode remain consumer responsibilities

comparison_rules.conversion: per required RGBA input: identical plane geometry; every Y/U/V sample within +-1 of the reference; exact-match fraction reported
comparison_rules.mux: independent re-demux (FFmpeg demuxer and an own TS checker) of both outputs: same PIDs, stream type (subject to the stream_type decision), PSI contents (subject to the SDT decision), PES payload bytes equal to the elementary stream, identical per-frame PTS/DTS/PCR, valid continuity, table cadence equal to the rule above; byte identity of the complete TS is checked when both get identical elementary streams
comparison_rules.encoder: v2 (revised 2026-11-02 before any native gate run): error-free independent FFmpeg decode of every frame; identical picture-type sequence; VBV underflow (H.262 Annex C variable-rate model, both streams simulated identically) no worse than the reference; and PSNR-Y over the common frames >= reference - 0.25 dB, judged (a) directly when the Rust stream uses <= 1.03x the reference bits, (b) directly when it uses more than that but <= 1.03x the requested budget (bit_rate x frames / 30), or (c) when the reference spent more than 1.03x the Rust bits, at equal bits: the Rust encoder is re-run at requested rates 1.25/1.6/2.0/2.6/3.4/4.5 x b until it reaches the reference's bits and its PSNR-Y is interpolated log-linearly at exactly the reference's bits; unreachable reference bits fail. Every report keeps the v1 verdict, the mode used and all points.
comparison_rules.pipeline: complete RGBA -> TS session: all three rules above on the same output
comparison_rules.runtime: paired, randomized-order, isolated native Linux ARM64; per case upper 95% bound of Rust/FFmpeg time ratio <= 1.25 (target 0.80)
comparison_rules.memory: per case, strictly lower peak live heap and strictly lower attributable RSS (harness/allocations-linux.c observer, separate runs)
comparison_rules.encoder_v1_superseded: independent FFmpeg decode of every frame succeeds with no decode errors; picture type sequence identical (I every 30, P otherwise); per case, PSNR-Y of the Rust output >= reference PSNR-Y - 0.25 dB at Rust bytes <= 1.03 * reference bytes over the same frame count, and VBV (maxrate, bufsize) never underflows under the H.262 Annex C model
comparison_rules.encoder_revision_reason: Exploratory local runs showed FFmpeg's short-session rate control lands far from the requested rate in both directions (content-limited UI pictures at qmin underspend; motion at 0.1-1 Mbps overspends up to 1.2x; noise exceeds the VBV by 26 Mbit), so v1's fixed '<= 1.03x reference bytes' made quality comparisons at unequal rates. v2 compares at equal bits where the reference overspent and permits spending within the client's requested budget where the reference underspent; clause (b) is a policy choice, approved under decisions, and results under it are labelled 'within-requested-budget'.

scope: latency: one frame of encoder delay and no final flush, as the reference
encoder rule v2, including clause (b) within the requested budget
